title: 241. Functions, Graphs & Transformations: Identifying Relations as Functions
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Definition of a Function from Ordered Pairs
questions.learningObjective: Identify which set of ordered pairs represents a function.
questions.question: Which set of ordered pairs represents a function?
questions.explanation: A relation is a function when each input is paired with exactly one output. In option A, each first coordinate \(1\), \(2\), \(3\), \(4\) appears exactly once. In option B, the input \(1\) is paired with both \(2\) and \(3\), so it is not a function. Therefore option A is correct.
questions.hint: Check whether any first coordinate is repeated with different second coordinates.

questions.concept: Function from a Table of Values
questions.learningObjective: Determine which table represents \(y\) as a function of \(x\).
questions.question: Which table represents \(y\) as a function of \(x\)?
questions.explanation: For \(y\) to be a function of \(x\), each \(x\)-value must correspond to exactly one \(y\)-value. In option B, the \(x\)-values \(1\), \(2\), \(3\), \(4\) are all different. In option A, the \(x\)-value \(2\) corresponds to both \(5\) and \(6\), so it is not a function. Therefore option B is correct.
questions.hint: Look for repeated \(x\)-values that have different \(y\)-values.

questions.learningObjective: Determine which equation defines \(y\) as a function of \(x\).
questions.question: Which equation defines \(y\) as a function of \(x\)?
questions.explanation: For \(y=x^2\), each input \(x\) gives exactly one output \(y\). For \(x=y^2\), if \(x=4\), then \(y=2\) or \(y=-2\), so one input gives two outputs. Therefore \(y=x^2\) defines \(y\) as a function of \(x\), and option B is correct.
questions.hint: Test whether a single \(x\)-value can produce more than one \(y\)-value.

questions.concept: Identifying a Non-Function from Ordered Pairs
questions.learningObjective: Select the relation that is not a function.
questions.question: Which relation is not a function?
questions.explanation: A relation is not a function if an input has more than one output. In option A, the input \(2\) is paired with \(5\) and \(7\), so it is not a function. In option B, each input appears exactly once, so it is a function. Therefore option A is correct.
questions.hint: Check whether one input value is paired with two different output values.

questions.learningObjective: Decide whether a mapping represents a function.
questions.question: In a mapping diagram, input \(3\) is assigned to output \(5\) and output \(8\). Is this relation a function?

options.label: A
options.text: Yes, because every input has at least one output.

options.label: B
options.text: No, because input \(3\) has two different outputs.

questions.explanation: A function must assign exactly one output to each input. Here input \(3\) is assigned to two outputs, \(5\) and \(8\). Therefore the relation is not a function, and option B is correct.
questions.hint: Inspect whether any single input points to more than one output.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the equation that represents \(y\) as a function of \(x\).
questions.question: Which equation represents \(y\) as a function of \(x\)?
questions.explanation: The equation \(y=3x+2\) gives exactly one \(y\)-value for each \(x\)-value, so it is a function. The equation \(x^2+y^2=9\) is a circle; for example, \(x=0\) gives \(y=3\) or \(y=-3\). Therefore option A is correct.
questions.hint: Determine whether any allowed \(x\)-value leads to two different \(y\)-values.

questions.learningObjective: Determine whether a relation with repeated outputs is a function.
questions.question: The relation \(R=\{(a,1),(b,2),(c,1),(d,3)\}\) is given. Is \(R\) a function?

options.label: A
options.text: No, because the output \(1\) appears more than once.

options.label: B
options.text: Yes, because each input has exactly one output.

questions.explanation: In a function, different inputs may share the same output. Here the inputs \(a\), \(b\), \(c\), \(d\) each appear exactly once, so each input has exactly one output. The repeated output \(1\) does not violate the definition of a function. Therefore option B is correct.
questions.hint: Focus on whether each input is used only once, not on repeated outputs.

questions.concept: Recognizing the Condition for a Non-Function
questions.learningObjective: Identify the statement that correctly describes when a relation is not a function.
questions.question: Which statement correctly describes a relation that is not a function?

options.label: A
options.text: At least one input value is paired with more than one output value.

options.label: B
options.text: At least one output value is paired with more than one input value.

questions.explanation: A relation fails to be a function when an input value is paired with more than one output value. Many different inputs sharing the same output value is allowed. Therefore option A is correct.
questions.hint: Recall that the function condition restricts each input, not each output.

questions.concept: Function from a Table with a Repeated Output
questions.learningObjective: Determine whether a table defines a function when an output value repeats.
questions.question: A relation is shown by the table: \(x:1,2,3,4\) and \(y:5,6,5,7\). Is this relation a function?

options.label: A
options.text: Yes, because every \(x\)-value appears exactly once.

questions.explanation: Each input \(x=1,2,3,4\) appears exactly once and is paired with exactly one output. The output \(5\) appearing twice for inputs \(1\) and \(3\) is allowed in a function. Therefore the relation is a function, and option A is correct.
questions.hint: Check the \(x\)-column for repeated values with different \(y\)-values.

questions.concept: Function from an Equation with Two Variables
questions.learningObjective: Identify an equation that does not define \(y\) as a function of \(x\).
questions.question: Which equation does not define \(y\) as a function of \(x\)?
questions.explanation: For \(x>0\), the equation \(|y|=x\) is satisfied by both \(y=x\) and \(y=-x\). For example, when \(x=2\), \(y=2\) or \(y=-2\), so one input gives two outputs. Thus \(y\) is not a function of \(x\). The equation \(y=x^3\) gives exactly one \(y\)-value for each \(x\)-value. Therefore option B is correct.
questions.hint: Look for an equation in which one \(x\)-value can correspond to two different \(y\)-values.
